# @fifthbell/brokaw

Server-side renderer and Handlebars template bundle for fifthbell pages.

## What it does

- Renders canonical content documents into HTML
- Supports every layout declared by the packaged Cronkite manifest, including
  article, homepage, category, search, 404, live-story, link-in-bio, media, and
  standalone pages
- Ships reusable Handlebars templates, partial dependency metadata, and compiled CSS
- Ships the complete Fifthbell live-program page, renderer media, local fonts, and a versioned integrity manifest
- Ships a CLS-owned social-image renderable and provider-neutral Remotion short-video renderable

## Installation

```bash
npm install @fifthbell/brokaw
```

## Basic usage

```ts
import { render } from "@fifthbell/brokaw";

const html = render(doc);
```

`doc` must match the normative canonical schema in
[src/schemas/canonical-document.schema.json](src/schemas/canonical-document.schema.json).
TypeScript declarations are generated from that schema; runtime rendering validates
against the same artifact.

### Optional real user monitoring

Public pages render without monitoring unless a complete `rumConfig` is supplied. The contract requires the public app monitor ID, application version, AWS region, Cognito identity pool ID, and guest role ARN. Brokaw validates the complete configuration and does not embed tenant deployment identifiers in the package.

When enabled, the shared standard and 404 shells collect only performance and filtered JavaScript-error telemetry. Page IDs use `window.location.pathname`; cookies, HTTP telemetry, resource URLs, X-Ray, and replay are disabled. Loader failures are isolated from page rendering and navigation.

## Exports

- `@fifthbell/brokaw` -> renderer entrypoint
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/cronkite-manifest.json` -> data-only CLS capability manifest
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/video` -> bundleable Remotion short-video entrypoint
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/schemas/canonical-document.schema.json` -> canonical input contract
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/schemas/cronkite-manifest.schema.json` -> CLS manifest contract
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/schemas/feed-renderable-input.schema.json` -> CMS-owned feed renderable input boundary
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/schemas/live-program-release-input.schema.json` -> generic live-program release input
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/partial-deps.json` -> partial-to-layout dependency map

The root module also exports `cronkiteManifest`, `outletConfig`, `version`,
`render`, `fontFiles`, `buildInstagramImageHtml`, and
`liveProgramReleaseFiles`. See [docs/cronkite-compatibility.md](docs/cronkite-compatibility.md)
for ownership, validation, system-page, asset, and release-ordering details.

## Fifthbell live-program bundle

`liveProgramPageFiles()` returns the deployable bundle as deterministic `{ key, body, contentType }` entries. It includes `index.html`, versioned JavaScript and CSS, every image/audio/font dependency, and `live-program-manifest.json`. The manifest records the Brokaw package version, renderer schema version, file byte sizes, content types, and SHA-256 digests. It is also an `alcantara.program-template` contract: it declares the renderer entrypoint, supported capabilities, accepted signals, and the runtime parameters Alcantara supplies. A publisher such as Cronkite must upload every returned key under the same public prefix; the relative URLs then work at any Cronkite-owned path.

`liveProgramReleaseFiles({ programId, apiBaseUrl })` is the manifest-declared
request renderable. It preserves the raw bundle export, emits versioned release
objects, and places the configured `html/program.html` commit point last.

```ts
import { liveProgramPageFiles } from "@fifthbell/brokaw";

for (const file of liveProgramPageFiles()) {
  await publish({
    key: file.key,
    body: file.body,
    contentType: file.contentType,
  });
}
```

The standalone renderer uses Alcantara's public, program-scoped contract:

- initial snapshot: `GET /program/:programId/state`
- updates: `GET /program/:programId/events` as server-sent events
- state ordering: the non-negative integer `version` supplied by Alcantara
- renderer schema: `schemaVersion: 1` when present; absent schema versions remain compatible with Alcantara's current v1 payload

Alcantara registers the versioned public URL of `live-program-manifest.json`, resolves the relative `entrypoint`, and uses the declared `capabilities` to expose only applicable controls. The `control.signals` allowlist is the complete set of SSE signal types this renderer accepts; adding renderer behavior requires updating that contract in the same release.

Cronkite can configure a published bundle at runtime by defining `window.__FIFTHBELL_LIVE_PROGRAM_CONFIG__ = { programId, apiBaseUrl }` before the module script runs, or by supplying `programId` and `apiBaseUrl` query parameters. Build-time `VITE_PROGRAM_ID` (default `fifthbell`) and `VITE_API_BASE_URL` are fallbacks. The API base can be an Alcantara origin, an origin ending in `/program`, or the complete `/program/:programId` endpoint; the complete endpoint form remains compatible with existing builds.

The renderer keeps its last valid state while SSE is unavailable, reconnects automatically, and fetches a fresh snapshot before consuming each new stream. Newer snapshots reconcile missed events; malformed, cross-program, incompatible-schema, stale, and out-of-order updates are ignored with a diagnostic console warning.

All presentation files are owned and packaged by Brokaw. Alcantara supplies state and events only; it is not an asset origin.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck
npm run test:unit
npm run build
npm run verify:packed-contract
npm pack --dry-run
npm run storybook
```

## Publish flow

- CI validates typecheck, unit tests, and package build on pull requests and `main` pushes.
- Package publish is triggered by pushing a `v*` tag.

### Mediathek

The `media-page` renderer emits one shared page for `/mediathek/<assignment-key>`.
Its browser script selects the assignment from the URL and fetches
`contents/assignments/<key>.json`; neither the HTML nor its canonical document is
assignment-specific. Storybook `Pages/MediaPage` uses Mediathek URLs.

## Pull request verification

Local agent review uses the shared `clouseau` skill with the developer's
authenticated coding harness and the `.clouseau-local.json` recipe; it needs no
CI provider keys. `AGENTS.md` owns the rule: run it against the final committed
change before opening a PR, repair findings, and publish the passing signed
receipt in the initial ready PR body. Never push directly to `main`.

Every PR runs:

- `npm run typecheck`,
- `npm run test:coverage`: the Vitest `unit` project under V8 coverage with exactly 100% line and branch coverage required over `src`,
- `npm run build` and the packed declarative contract check (`node scripts/verify-packed-contract.mjs`),
- the workflow-contract tests in `.github/tests`.

The Clouseau gate requires exactly 100% line and branch coverage over every
non-test file in `src`; new behaviour needs a test, never a coverage pragma.
Until the suite reaches that bar the coverage step fails, so a PR stays in
human review and is merged by the owner rather than automatically.

A PR carrying an authenticated local review stamp is verified by the pinned
Clouseau engine without AI credentials; unstamped PRs use the CI reviewer.
Passing reviews receive a bot approval and native auto-merge. Unresolved
product-direction questions go to the owner, and changes to review controls need
the owner's `/approve-intent <head SHA>` comment. See [the purpose
contract](.github/clouseau.md). The CI engine is resolved from protected
Clouseau `main` at the start of each run (see
[automatic Clouseau CI upgrades](https://github.com/gaulatti/clouseau/blob/main/docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md)).

Package publication and the Storybook deployment stay separate, explicitly
authorized workflows outside this review contract.

CI needs these repository secrets: `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` for
the CI reviewer, and `DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN` (a token with contents write access
from an identity other than `github-actions[bot]`) for automatic repairs.

# Brokaw review contract

Brokaw (`@fifthbell/brokaw`) is the server-side renderer and Handlebars template bundle for Fifthbell pages. It
renders canonical content documents into HTML for every layout declared by the
packaged Cronkite manifest, and ships the templates, partial dependency
metadata, compiled CSS, fonts and the live-program page that downstream
publishing consumes as a versioned npm package.

Preserve the rendering contract: the packaged manifest and its layouts, the
declarative templates and explicit partial dependencies, the canonical document
shape, the packed declarative contract that consumers verify, and the
integrity manifest of shipped assets. A change to a template, layout or
renderer needs a Storybook story or test that shows the output a consumer sees,
as `AGENTS.md` requires. Bug fixes, meaningful tests, accessibility,
documentation and dependency maintenance serve this existing package without a
new product decision. A new layout, a breaking contract change or a new
runtime dependency needs documentation or a linked requirement that establishes
its need and boundaries. Package publication and the Storybook deployment stay
separate, explicitly authorized workflows outside this review contract.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision.
Ordinary implementation uncertainty and repairable bugs belong to automated
investigation, not routine human code review. Changes to review controls (this
contract, `.github/clouseau.json`, the CI workflow, the local recipe) require
explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80
for fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal
technical finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores
cannot average away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain
independent.

Tests must assert actual rendered output or contract behaviour. Reject
fabricated coverage, disabled tests, coverage pragmas or exclusions, swallowed
errors, unconditional assertions and mocks that replace the behaviour being
claimed. The type check, unit tests, package build and packed-contract
verification remain mandatory, and every pull request must keep exactly 100%
line and branch coverage of `src`; a pull request below that stays for human
review.

# AI Agentic Update

Refresh only the current repository from the authoritative `bastille`
repository.

## Required action

Run this skill's deterministic updater before substantive repository work:

```bash
.agents/skills/ai-agentic-update/scripts/update
```

If the current directory is below the repository root, resolve the repository
root first and execute the script from there. After a successful update, reread
the root `AGENTS.md` and any applicable updated skills before continuing.

The helper fetches the central repository, hydrates the current repository from
the fetched default-branch snapshot, creates a narrowly scoped Conventional
Commit when managed files changed, and verifies the result. Wiki management
applies only to public repositories, determined from the GitHub visibility of
the repository's `origin`: it verifies the repository's separate `./wiki`
checkout, clones the wiki when its derived remote exists, and validates an
existing checkout's origin. Private repositories are skipped unless a `./wiki`
checkout already exists, in which case it is preserved and kept current. It
preserves instructions outside the managed markers, differently named local
skills, uncommitted wiki work, and unrelated product changes. Its commit owns
only `AGENTS.md`, the managed-skills manifest, and centrally owned skill paths;
it must not absorb staged or unstaged product files.

Do not replace this command with hand-written copying. After it completes,
inspect the relevant wiki pages in public repositories before planning code
changes. Do not separately commit the refresh or carry its files into the
product change. If its scoped commit fails, stop rather than continuing with
dirty managed metadata. The updater does not push, deploy, reset, rebase, or
discard product or wiki work.

If the fetched revision changes the updater implementation, the current process
hands off once to a temporary copy of the fetched updater. A guard prevents
handoff loops and makes a failure visible. The central sync also recognizes the
exact no-commit call made by pre-commit legacy updaters and creates the required
narrow bootstrap commit during that same first invocation; this compatibility
does not make ordinary manual `sync --write --repository` calls commit.

Access to private bastille must not block agent execution. If central fetch or
clone fails because access or connectivity is unavailable, the updater reports
`bastille-unavailable` and uses the complete checked-in managed snapshot without
changing it. Continue with that snapshot; no private-repository credential is
required of contributors. Report the unavailable refresh in the handoff.

Malformed or incomplete installed metadata, conflicting ownership, unsafe central
content, and failed managed commits still stop work and must be reported. Do not
invent a new snapshot or ignore these errors. Initial installation without a
committed snapshot needs an authorized maintainer.

For a task worktree already stopped by the legacy dirty-metadata failure, do not
blindly invoke the updater again. Preserve unrelated work and restart the ticket
from a fresh current-default-branch worktree after the compatibility release is
published.

An explicit invocation authorizes the updater's fetch and its narrowly scoped
changes to the central checkout/cache and current repository. It does not
authorize any other external or destructive action.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -euo pipefail

readonly CANONICAL_REMOTE='git@github.com:gaulatti/bastille.git'

TARGET_REPOSITORY=''
REFERENCE_REPOSITORY="${BASTILLE_REPOSITORY:-}"
FETCH='true'

usage() {
  printf '%s\n' 'Usage: update [--repository PATH] [--reference-repository PATH] [--no-fetch]'
}

wiki_remote_from_origin() {
  local origin_url="$1"
  if [[ "${origin_url}" == *.git ]]; then
    printf '%s.wiki.git\n' "${origin_url%.git}"
  else
    printf '%s.wiki.git\n' "${origin_url}"
  fi
}

github_slug_from_url() {
  local url="$1"
  local slug=''
  local owner=''
  local repo=''
  case "${url}" in
    git@github.com:*)
      slug="${url#git@github.com:}"
      ;;
    git@github.com/*)
      slug="${url#git@github.com/}"
      ;;
    ssh://git@github.com:*)
      slug="${url#ssh://git@github.com:}"
      ;;
    ssh://git@github.com/*)
      slug="${url#ssh://git@github.com/}"
      ;;
    https://github.com/*)
      slug="${url#https://github.com/}"
      ;;
    http://github.com/*)
      slug="${url#http://github.com/}"
      ;;
    *)
      return 0
      ;;
  esac
  slug="${slug#/}"
  slug="${slug%/}"
  slug="${slug%.git}"
  owner="${slug%%/*}"
  repo="${slug#*/}"
  repo="${repo%%/*}"
  if [[ -n "${owner}" && -n "${repo}" ]]; then
    printf '%s/%s\n' "${owner}" "${repo}"
  fi
}

repository_visibility() {
  local repository="$1"
  local origin_url=''
  local slug=''
  local visibility=''
  origin_url="$(git -C "${repository}" config --get remote.origin.url 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [[ -z "${origin_url}" ]]; then
    printf 'unknown\n'
    return 0
  fi
  slug="$(github_slug_from_url "${origin_url}")"
  if [[ -z "${slug}" ]]; then
    printf 'unknown\n'
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && visibility="$(gh repo view "${slug}" --json visibility --jq .visibility 2>/dev/null)"; then
    printf '%s\n' "${visibility}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'
  else
    printf 'unknown\n'
  fi
}

ensure_wiki_checkout() {
  local repository="$1"
  local wiki_directory="${repository}/wiki"
  local origin_url=''
  local wiki_remote=''
  local existing_remote=''
  local exclude_file=''
  local wiki_branch=''
  local visibility=''

  origin_url="$(git -C "${repository}" config --get remote.origin.url 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [[ -z "${origin_url}" ]]; then
    printf 'wiki-unavailable\trepository=%s\treason=no-origin\n' "${repository}"
    return 0
  fi
  wiki_remote="$(wiki_remote_from_origin "${origin_url}")"

  visibility="$(repository_visibility "${repository}")"
  if [[ "${visibility}" != 'public' && "${visibility}" != 'unknown' \
    && ! -d "${wiki_directory}/.git" ]]; then
    printf 'wiki-skip\trepository=%s\tvisibility=%s\treason=non-public-repository\n' \
      "${repository}" "${visibility}"
    return 0
  fi

  exclude_file="$(git -C "${repository}" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path info/exclude)"
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "${exclude_file}")"
  touch "${exclude_file}"
  if ! grep -Fqx '/wiki/' "${exclude_file}"; then
    printf '\n/wiki/\n' >> "${exclude_file}"
  fi

  if [[ -e "${wiki_directory}" && ! -d "${wiki_directory}/.git" ]]; then
    printf 'error: ./wiki exists but is not a Git checkout: %s\n' "${wiki_directory}" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  if [[ ! -d "${wiki_directory}/.git" ]]; then
    if GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git clone --quiet "${wiki_remote}" "${wiki_directory}" 2>/dev/null; then
      printf 'wiki-cloned\trepository=%s\tremote=%s\n' "${repository}" "${wiki_remote}"
      return 0
    fi
    rm -rf "${wiki_directory}"
    printf 'wiki-unavailable\trepository=%s\tremote=%s\treason=remote-not-found-or-inaccessible\n' \
      "${repository}" "${wiki_remote}"
    return 0
  fi

  existing_remote="$(git -C "${wiki_directory}" config --get remote.origin.url 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [[ "${existing_remote}" != "${wiki_remote}" ]]; then
    printf 'error: ./wiki origin mismatch: expected %s, found %s\n' \
      "${wiki_remote}" "${existing_remote:-no-origin}" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  if ! GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git -C "${wiki_directory}" fetch --quiet origin --prune 2>/dev/null; then
    printf 'wiki-unavailable\trepository=%s\tremote=%s\treason=fetch-failed\n' \
      "${repository}" "${wiki_remote}"
    return 0
  fi

  if [[ -n "$(git -C "${wiki_directory}" status --porcelain)" ]]; then
    printf 'wiki-current\trepository=%s\tstate=dirty-preserved\n' "${repository}"
    return 0
  fi

  wiki_branch="$(git -C "${wiki_directory}" branch --show-current)"
  if [[ -n "${wiki_branch}" ]] && git -C "${wiki_directory}" show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/remotes/origin/${wiki_branch}"; then
    if git -C "${wiki_directory}" merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD "refs/remotes/origin/${wiki_branch}"; then
      git -C "${wiki_directory}" merge --ff-only --quiet "refs/remotes/origin/${wiki_branch}"
    fi
  fi
  printf 'wiki-current\trepository=%s\tremote=%s\n' "${repository}" "${wiki_remote}"
}

installed_managed_block() {
  awk '
    /^<!-- BEGIN (BASTILLE|AGENTIC-CODING) MANAGED RULES -->$/ {
      if (inside || seen++) exit 1
      inside = 1
      expected = $0
      sub(/BEGIN/, "END", expected)
    }
    inside { print }
    /^<!-- END (BASTILLE|AGENTIC-CODING) MANAGED RULES -->$/ {
      if (!inside || $0 != expected) exit 1
      inside = 0
      complete++
    }
    END { if (inside || seen != 1 || complete != 1) exit 1 }
  '
}

use_installed_standard() {
  local installed=''
  local committed=''
  local manifest='.agents/skills/.bastille-managed'
  local legacy='.agents/skills/.agentic-coding-managed'
  local skill=''
  local paths=()

  if ! installed="$(installed_managed_block < "${TARGET_REPOSITORY}/AGENTS.md")" \
    || ! committed="$(git -C "${TARGET_REPOSITORY}" show HEAD:AGENTS.md 2>/dev/null | installed_managed_block)" \
    || [[ "${installed}" != "${committed}" ]]; then
    printf 'error: central access unavailable and no complete unchanged checked-in managed rules exist: %s\n' "${TARGET_REPOSITORY}" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if [[ ! -f "${TARGET_REPOSITORY}/${manifest}" ]]; then
    manifest="${legacy}"
  elif [[ -f "${TARGET_REPOSITORY}/${legacy}" ]] \
    && ! cmp -s "${TARGET_REPOSITORY}/${manifest}" "${TARGET_REPOSITORY}/${legacy}"; then
    printf 'error: central access unavailable and installed manifests conflict: %s\n' "${TARGET_REPOSITORY}" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  if [[ ! -f "${TARGET_REPOSITORY}/${manifest}" ]]; then
    printf 'error: central access unavailable and installed skill ownership is missing: %s\n' "${TARGET_REPOSITORY}" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  paths+=("${manifest}")
  while IFS= read -r skill; do
    [[ -z "${skill}" ]] && continue
    if [[ ! "${skill}" =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$ ]] \
      || [[ ! -f "${TARGET_REPOSITORY}/.agents/skills/${skill}/SKILL.md" ]]; then
      printf 'error: central access unavailable and installed skill metadata is invalid: %s\n' "${TARGET_REPOSITORY}" >&2
      return 1
    fi

    ssh://git@github.com/*)

      ;;

# @fifthbell/brokaw

Server-side renderer and Handlebars template bundle for fifthbell pages.

## What it does

- Renders canonical content documents into HTML
- Supports every layout declared by the packaged Cronkite manifest, including
  article, homepage, category, search, 404, live-story, link-in-bio, media, and
  standalone pages
- Ships reusable Handlebars templates, partial dependency metadata, and compiled CSS
- Ships the complete Fifthbell live-program page, renderer media, local fonts, and a versioned integrity manifest
- Ships a CLS-owned social-image renderable and provider-neutral Remotion short-video renderable

## Installation

```bash
npm install @fifthbell/brokaw
```

## Basic usage

```ts
import { render } from "@fifthbell/brokaw";

const html = render(doc);
```

`doc` must match the normative canonical schema in
[src/schemas/canonical-document.schema.json](src/schemas/canonical-document.schema.json).
TypeScript declarations are generated from that schema; runtime rendering validates
against the same artifact.

### Optional real user monitoring

Public pages render without monitoring unless a complete `rumConfig` is supplied. The contract requires the public app monitor ID, application version, AWS region, Cognito identity pool ID, and guest role ARN. Brokaw validates the complete configuration and does not embed tenant deployment identifiers in the package.

When enabled, the shared standard and 404 shells collect only performance and filtered JavaScript-error telemetry. Page IDs use `window.location.pathname`; cookies, HTTP telemetry, resource URLs, X-Ray, and replay are disabled. Loader failures are isolated from page rendering and navigation.

## Exports

- `@fifthbell/brokaw` -> renderer entrypoint
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/cronkite-manifest.json` -> data-only CLS capability manifest
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/video` -> bundleable Remotion short-video entrypoint
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/schemas/canonical-document.schema.json` -> canonical input contract
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/schemas/cronkite-manifest.schema.json` -> CLS manifest contract
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/schemas/feed-renderable-input.schema.json` -> CMS-owned feed renderable input boundary
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/schemas/live-program-release-input.schema.json` -> generic live-program release input
- `@fifthbell/brokaw/partial-deps.json` -> partial-to-layout dependency map

The root module also exports `cronkiteManifest`, `outletConfig`, `version`,
`render`, `fontFiles`, `buildInstagramImageHtml`, and
`liveProgramReleaseFiles`. See [docs/cronkite-compatibility.md](docs/cronkite-compatibility.md)
for ownership, validation, system-page, asset, and release-ordering details.

## Fifthbell live-program bundle

`liveProgramPageFiles()` returns the deployable bundle as deterministic `{ key, body, contentType }` entries. It includes `index.html`, versioned JavaScript and CSS, every image/audio/font dependency, and `live-program-manifest.json`. The manifest records the Brokaw package version, renderer schema version, file byte sizes, content types, and SHA-256 digests. It is also an `alcantara.program-template` contract: it declares the renderer entrypoint, supported capabilities, accepted signals, and the runtime parameters Alcantara supplies. A publisher such as Cronkite must upload every returned key under the same public prefix; the relative URLs then work at any Cronkite-owned path.

`liveProgramReleaseFiles({ programId, apiBaseUrl })` is the manifest-declared
request renderable. It preserves the raw bundle export, emits versioned release
objects, and places the configured `html/program.html` commit point last.

```ts
import { liveProgramPageFiles } from "@fifthbell/brokaw";

for (const file of liveProgramPageFiles()) {
  await publish({
    key: file.key,
    body: file.body,
    contentType: file.contentType,
  });
}
```

The standalone renderer uses Alcantara's public, program-scoped contract:

- initial snapshot: `GET /program/:programId/state`
- updates: `GET /program/:programId/events` as server-sent events
- state ordering: the non-negative integer `version` supplied by Alcantara
- renderer schema: `schemaVersion: 1` when present; absent schema versions remain compatible with Alcantara's current v1 payload

Alcantara registers the versioned public URL of `live-program-manifest.json`, resolves the relative `entrypoint`, and uses the declared `capabilities` to expose only applicable controls. The `control.signals` allowlist is the complete set of SSE signal types this renderer accepts; adding renderer behavior requires updating that contract in the same release.

Cronkite can configure a published bundle at runtime by defining `window.__FIFTHBELL_LIVE_PROGRAM_CONFIG__ = { programId, apiBaseUrl }` before the module script runs, or by supplying `programId` and `apiBaseUrl` query parameters. Build-time `VITE_PROGRAM_ID` (default `fifthbell`) and `VITE_API_BASE_URL` are fallbacks. The API base can be an Alcantara origin, an origin ending in `/program`, or the complete `/program/:programId` endpoint; the complete endpoint form remains compatible with existing builds.

The renderer keeps its last valid state while SSE is unavailable, reconnects automatically, and fetches a fresh snapshot before consuming each new stream. Newer snapshots reconcile missed events; malformed, cross-program, incompatible-schema, stale, and out-of-order updates are ignored with a diagnostic console warning.

All presentation files are owned and packaged by Brokaw. Alcantara supplies state and events only; it is not an asset origin.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run typecheck
npm run test:unit
npm run build
npm run verify:packed-contract
npm pack --dry-run
npm run storybook
```

## Publish flow

- CI validates typecheck, unit tests, and package build on pull requests and `main` pushes.
- Package publish is triggered by pushing a `v*` tag.

### Mediathek

The `media-page` renderer emits one shared page for `/mediathek/<assignment-key>`.
Its browser script selects the assignment from the URL and fetches
`contents/assignments/<key>.json`; neither the HTML nor its canonical document is
assignment-specific. Storybook `Pages/MediaPage` uses Mediathek URLs.

Every `media-page` document must supply `assignmentMediaBaseUrl`: a completed
absolute HTTP(S) directory ending in `/contents/assignments/`, including its
trailing slash, without credentials, query or fragment. The browser appends only
the encoded opaque assignment key and `.json`; it does not infer an origin from
the page URL or use a package fallback. The static manifest document explicitly
supplies Fifthbell's preview value. Cronkite replaces it from its configured
tenant CDN directory for basement publication; a direct CMS render supplies its
own completed value.

The manifest declares this shell as a single `media-page` system variant at
`html/mediathek/index.html`. A basement refresh publishes it alongside search,
404 pages, and static assets. Ariston's successful-publication receipt handler
requests that refresh when it detects a new CLS version. Restarting Cronkite
loads npm `latest`; publication follows the CMS refresh, rather than startup.
Storybook `Pages/MediaPage/SharedSystemPage` previews the manifest document.

Local packed-consumer checks verify the source candidate; they do not publish or
adopt it. The current-main `0.1.72` article candidate and the earlier Mediathek
`0.1.72` rehearsal have different contents. A combined package needs its own
reviewed release artifact and explicit publication decision before normal
Cronkite adoption and the CMS-triggered refresh are verified together.

## Pull request verification

Local agent review uses the shared `clouseau` skill with the developer's
authenticated coding harness and the `.clouseau-local.json` recipe; it needs no
CI provider keys. `AGENTS.md` owns the rule: run it against the final committed
change before opening a PR, repair findings, and publish the passing signed
receipt in the initial ready PR body. Never push directly to `main`.

Every PR runs:

- `npm run typecheck`,
- `npm run test:coverage`: the Vitest `unit` project under V8 coverage with exactly 100% line and branch coverage required over `src`,
- `npm run build` and the packed declarative contract check (`node scripts/verify-packed-contract.mjs`),
- the workflow-contract tests in `.github/tests`.

The Clouseau gate requires exactly 100% line and branch coverage over every
non-test file in `src`; new behaviour needs a test, never a coverage pragma.
Until the suite reaches that bar the coverage step fails, so a PR stays in
human review and is merged by the owner rather than automatically.

A PR carrying an authenticated local review stamp is verified by the pinned
Clouseau engine without AI credentials; unstamped PRs use the CI reviewer.
Passing reviews receive a bot approval and native auto-merge. Unresolved
product-direction questions go to the owner, and changes to review controls need
the owner's `/approve-intent <head SHA>` comment. See [the purpose
contract](.github/clouseau.md). The CI engine is resolved from protected
Clouseau `main` at the start of each run (see
[automatic Clouseau CI upgrades](https://github.com/gaulatti/clouseau/blob/main/docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md)).

Package publication and the Storybook deployment stay separate, explicitly
authorized workflows outside this review contract.

CI needs these repository secrets: `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` for
the CI reviewer, and `DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN` (a token with contents write access
from an identity other than `github-actions[bot]`) for automatic repairs.

# Cronkite compatibility

Brokaw publishes the pinned declarative template contract for Fifthbell. The
source artifact is `src/cronkite-manifest.ts`; the build validates it against
`src/schemas/cronkite-manifest.schema.json` and emits
`dist/cronkite-manifest.json`.

The emitted artifact has only three top-level members: `package`, `version`,
and `templateRendering`. Cronkite compiles the declared Handlebars entries and
partial graph directly. Publishing an HTML page no longer requires importing or
executing `dist/renderer.js`.

## Complete document boundary

Every page renderable validates the supplied document against the packed
canonical-document schema. The CMS owns the completed rendering input,
including:

- canonical URLs and article/reference URLs;
- pre-distributed `homepageSlots` and explicit homepage visibility flags;
- `logoLink`, `statusVariant`, and localized `searchCopy` when applicable;
- structured `seo.socialImage` data;
- extracted vendor identifiers such as `tweetId` and TikTok `videoId`;
- optional, validated public RUM configuration.

The browser and Node renderers remain as local and Storybook compatibility
exports. They render the same completed document without composing editorial
state or deriving vendor identifiers.

## Templates, helpers, and embeds

The manifest names every direct partial dependency in source order. Dynamic
partials, inline partial decorators, and partial blocks have been replaced by
ordinary declared partials so Cronkite can validate the graph before serving
requests.

Templates use only the pinned helpers: `eq`, `add`, `slice`, `uppercase`,
`coalesce`, `jsonString`, `embedUrl`, `formatDate`,
`socialImageUrl`, and `socialImageAlt`. X, TikTok, Instagram, and SofaScore
URL shapes are data in `embedRegistry`, not executable package helpers. The
social-card template accepts caller-supplied `qrCodeHtml`; QR generation is
not part of declarative rendering.

SofaScore embeds are optional. Live-story and breaking-news templates guard
the entire embed section on `sofascore_id` and expand both URLs without
changing the document context. A missing identifier omits the section; it is
never passed to Cronkite's fail-closed `embedUrl` helper.

The conditional RUM loader is a declared Handlebars partial. It retains
pathname-only page IDs, strips resource performance entries, disables cookies,
X-Ray, resource URLs, and automatic page views, and rejects sensitive error
payloads without requiring a JavaScript renderer import.

## System pages and localization

The manifest declares 404 and search pages as explicit English, Spanish, and
Italian variants. English is Fifthbell's default language, so its object keys
and routes are unprefixed:

- `html/404/index.html` at `/404`;
- `html/search/index.html` at `/search`.

Spanish and Italian variants retain `/es/` and `/it/` prefixes. Each variant
contains a complete document. Search headings, controls, empty states, result
messages, pagination, loading text, and failure text come from the document's
localized `searchCopy`. `outletConfig.searchTitle` is no longer part of the
contract.

## Static and raster assets

The manifest maps every packed font, the font stylesheet, and the compiled
Brokaw stylesheet to exact output keys with content types and immutable cache
policy. Page shells link to the published stylesheet instead of expecting CSS
to be injected by renderer code.

The `social-image` renderable retains JPEG rasterization at 1080 by 1350. Its
input schema requires `imageUrl`, `categoryName`, `title`, and
caller-supplied `qrCodeHtml`.

Brokaw's legacy live-program and short-video exports remain available to their
existing direct consumers, but they are not members of the declarative page
artifact.

`npm run build` validates and emits the artifact, copies schemas and fonts,
and verifies the retained live-program bundle. Unit tests cover schema
validation, manifest alignment, explicit system-page keys and routes, static
assets, embed data, and output parity between declarative rendering and the
legacy local renderer for article, homepage, category, search, and link-in-bio
documents. `npm run build-storybook` verifies the updated page, partial, RUM,
standalone-page, and social-image stories.

The article page fills the available width and keeps its header, update notice,
share controls and body inside the explicit grid with `col-span-full`. A fixed
twelve-column span at the mobile one-column breakpoint creates implicit tracks
and can make the text wider than a narrow reading frame. Desktop-specific image,
share and body spans retain their existing twelve-column placement.

headlines, excerpts and body text can wrap without changing or truncating the
supplied words. Every canonical `authors[].name` appears in supplied order using
the existing editorial metadata style. Handlebars escapes names as text. An empty
author array omits the byline. The existing publication date and canonical input
requirements remain in force; these changes retain template contract version 1
and add no required document fields.

`Pages/Article reading` supplies deterministic published `PublishedStory`,
`WithLeadImage`, `WithUpdatedVersion`, `LongUnbrokenHeadline` and `MultipleAuthors`
stories without a preview-data service. Inspect direct story iframes at 236px,
306px, 390px, 768px and 1440px. Check the opening paragraph, quote, attribution,
closing paragraph, supplied image URL, optional update notice and desktop
share/body placement. Rendered-markup regressions verify these boundaries and
author escaping; browser layout acceptance must also exercise the generated CSS.

stories and widths. The complete story, lead image, update notice, wrapping,
ordered byline and desktop share/body placement remained within the article
frame. At 390px and 1440px, native Tab/Shift+Tab traversal reached the eight
share links and the updated-version link with visible focus; no link was
activated.

The check used native Chrome's responsive Desktop engine at 50% preview, with
actual toolbar widths and screenshots checked. Physical-device and VoiceOver
acceptance were outside that check. A local favicon 404 was observed; the
record makes no globally clean-console claim. The shared shell retains its
existing public fixed-city weather requests. Screenshots were emitted in the

SHA-256 `692322950b8adf2b411bc1e40acb9222e3489b2f0ea5356f7cb05def48d9b805`.
These are local acceptance results; the separate delivery steps below still
apply.

This repair needs both the package templates and the compiled stylesheet.
The page shell continues to request the established published Brokaw stylesheet.
At release preparation on 17 October 2026, that served stylesheet already
contained the full-span and width utilities needed for the grid repair, but did
not contain `wrap-anywhere` or an `overflow-wrap:anywhere` declaration. The grid
correction can use those existing rules; the complete long-word repair requires
activation of the newly generated stylesheet.
Publishing an npm package alone does not activate its CSS or change existing
article HTML. Release verification must confirm the selected consumer accepts
the contract-1 package, deliver its generated CSS through the existing static-asset

affected articles, and inspect the final public output and cache activation.

telemetry change in this repair. The public wiki remote was unavailable, so this

- Ships reusable Handlebars templates, partial dependency metadata, and compiled CSS
- Ships the complete Fifthbell live-program page, renderer media, local fonts, and a versioned integrity manifest

```bash
npm install @fifthbell/brokaw
```

```ts

const html = render(doc);
```

`doc` must match the normative canonical schema in

TypeScript declarations are generated from that schema; runtime rendering validates
against the same artifact.

### Optional real user monitoring

Public pages render without monitoring unless a complete `rumConfig` is supplied. The contract requires the public app monitor ID, application version, AWS region, Cognito identity pool ID, and guest role ARN. Brokaw validates the complete configuration and does not embed tenant deployment identifiers in the package.

When enabled, the shared standard and 404 shells collect only performance and filtered JavaScript-error telemetry. Page IDs use `window.location.pathname`; cookies, HTTP telemetry, resource URLs, X-Ray, and replay are disabled. Loader failures are isolated from page rendering and navigation.

The `control.signals` allowlist is the complete set of SSE signal types this renderer accepts; adding renderer behavior requires updating that contract in the same release.

Cronkite can configure a published bundle at runtime by defining `window.__FIFTHBELL_LIVE_PROGRAM_CONFIG__ = { programId, apiBaseUrl }` before the module script runs, or by supplying `programId` and `apiBaseUrl` query parameters. The API base can be an Alcantara origin, an origin ending in `/program`, or the complete `/program/:programId` endpoint; the complete endpoint form remains compatible with existing builds.

The renderer keeps its last valid state while SSE is unavailable, reconnects automatically, and fetches a fresh snapshot before consuming each new stream. Newer snapshots reconcile missed events; malformed, cross-program, incompatible-schema, stale, and out-of-order updates are ignored with a diagnostic console warning.

All presentation files are owned and packaged by Brokaw. Alcantara supplies state and events only; it is not an asset origin.
